page.layout: Running head at top, with page number at the top left. Continuous text in one column, with a heading "CAPITIS I." and "SECTIO III." set centred. A marginal note in the left margin beside the opening paragraph. No text at the foot except a catchword at the bottom right.

main_text.p: linquat. Merito puniuntur & impe-nitentes victimam Christi rejicientes, & sanguinem ejus pedibus conculcan-tes, sed ut fiat condonatio peccatorum, fuit necesse sponsore nostrum, in quem Deus conjecerat iniquitates omnium nostrum, dolores nostros portare, & poenas nostris peccatis debitas perferre, ut ejus obedientia & meritum credenti-bus per fidem in ipsum imputaretur. Sed prolixior in hoc argumento meditando fui, ad aliud me converte.
main_text.head: CAPITIS I.
SECTIO III.
main_text.p: 3. Objectio. Nobis non pereuntibus non potest justitia Dei satisfieri.Si pro peccatis satisfactione est opus, nobis peccatoribus erit necessario pereundum.
At nobis non est necessario omnibus pereundum.
Ergo pro peccatis satisfactione non est opus.
Si Deus aut non potuisset, aut noluisset, citra veram aliquam pro delictis nostris satisfactionem nobis ignoscere, nos ipsi omnino ei satisfacere debuissemus. Neque enim aliquid Deo dr-

page.notes: The page number reads "2i2", probably 212, so it is marked [?]. The running head is printed as "II. LIBER: SOCINIA-" with the word continued across the line; I have completed it as SOCINIANORUM. The catchword at the bottom right is a partly legible hyphenated word and could not be read with confidence. The line "Neque enim aliquid Deo dr-" is cut off at the page edge and the continuation is not visible. The end of "converte" carries a dingbat mark which is not transcribed. The word "Deo" after "aliquid" is printed in a damaged form and is not certain.
